questions.question: In the context of Lipids, what is the major organic product when Glyceryl tripalmitate (Tripalmitin) reacts under the following conditions: 3.0 equiv NaOH(aq), 100°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Base-promoted hydrolysis of triglyceride triesters yields glycerol and three fatty acid soap carboxylate salts. The correct major product is 'Glycerol + 3 Sodium palmitate [CH₃(CH₂)₁₄COO⁻Na⁺] (Soap)'.

questions.question: In the context of Lipids, what is the major organic product when Glyceryl trioleate (Liquid oil with 3 cis-C=C) reacts under the following conditions: Excess H₂ / Ni catalyst, 180°C?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Hydrogenation of cis-double bonds in unsaturated fatty acid chains raises melting point, hardening liquid oil into solid fat. The correct major product is 'Glyceryl tristearate (Tristearin, solid saturated fat)'.

questions.question: In the context of Lipids, what is the major organic product when Oleic acid [cis-CH₃(CH₂)₇CH=CH(CH₂)₇COOH] reacts under the following conditions: Br₂ in dry CCl₄?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Electrophilic anti addition of bromine across the cis-double bond decolors the red-brown bromine solution. The correct major product is '9,10-Dibromooctadecanoic acid'.

questions.question: In the context of Lipids, what is the major organic product when Phosphatidylcholine (Lecithin) reacts under the following conditions: Phospholipase A₂ / aqueous buffer?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Enzymatic cleavage selectively hydrolyzes the ester bond at the C2 position of the glycerol backbone. The correct major product is 'Lysophosphatidylcholine + Free fatty acid (at C2)'.

questions.question: In the context of Lipids, what is the major organic product when 2 Isoprene units (C₅H₈) reacts under the following conditions: Biosynthetic coupling (DMAPP + IPP)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Head-to-tail biosynthetic coupling of two activated 5-carbon isoprene pyrophosphates forms cyclic monoterpene limonene. The correct major product is 'Limonene (C₁₀H₁₆, Monoterpene)'.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Cholesterol (3β-Hydroxy-5-cholestene) into 4-Cholesten-3-one (via oxidation and alkene migration) in Lipids?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Cholesterol (3β-Hydroxy-5-cholestene)' → '4-Cholesten-3-one (via oxidation and alkene migration)' specifically requires 'CrO₃ / H₂SO₄ in acetone (Jones reagent)'. Mechanistic basis: Oxidizes the 3β-hydroxyl group to a ketone with simultaneous double bond migration into conjugation with the carbonyl.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Cholesterol into Cholesteryl acetate + Acetic acid in Lipids?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Cholesterol' → 'Cholesteryl acetate + Acetic acid' specifically requires 'Acetic anhydride / Pyridine, 25°C'. Mechanistic basis: Selective esterification of the secondary C3 hydroxyl group on the steroid A-ring.

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert Squalene 2,3-epoxide into Lanosterol (Tetracyclic steroid precursor) in Lipids?
questions.explanation: Reagent selection rationale: The transformation 'Squalene 2,3-epoxide' → 'Lanosterol (Tetracyclic steroid precursor)' specifically requires 'Oxidosqualene cyclase enzyme in vivo'. Mechanistic basis: Tandem cationic cascade cyclizes linear squalene epoxide into the 4-ring cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene steroid skeleton.

questions.question: Which starting material yields 'Prostaglandin H₂ (PGH₂ with cyclopentane endoperoxide)' when treated with 'Cyclooxygenase (COX) + 2 O₂' according to the principles of Lipids?
questions.explanation: Starting material deduction: Treating 'Arachidonic acid (C₂₀:4 ω-6)' with 'Cyclooxygenase (COX) + 2 O₂' yields 'Prostaglandin H₂ (PGH₂ with cyclopentane endoperoxide)'. Mechanistic rationale: Enzymatic oxygenation and cyclization of arachidonic acid generates the cyclopentane core of prostaglandins.

questions.question: Which starting material yields 'Methyl palmitate + 1-Hexadecanol (Cetyl alcohol)' when treated with '1.0 M NaOH / CH₃OH, 70°C' according to the principles of Lipids?
questions.explanation: Starting material deduction: Treating 'Cetyl palmitate [CH₃(CH₂)₁₄COO(CH₂)₁₅CH₃] (Spermaceti wax)' with '1.0 M NaOH / CH₃OH, 70°C' yields 'Methyl palmitate + 1-Hexadecanol (Cetyl alcohol)'. Mechanistic rationale: Base-catalyzed methanolysis cleaves the long-chain wax ester into a fatty acid methyl ester and long-chain alcohol.
